newsitem.title: YEMEN: Infant mortality drops in Yemen, UNICEF says.
newsitem.headline: Infant mortality drops in Yemen, UNICEF says.

text.p: Infant mortality in impoverished Yemen is expected to drop to 110 in every 1,000 births in 1997 from 400 in 1960, an annual UNICEF report on children said.
The report was distributed on Thursday by U.N. Children's Fund (UNICEF) representative in Yemen, Carl Tinstman.
He told reporters UNICEF was working with Yemeni authorities to reduce mortality among children under five-years-old to 60 in every 1,000 births.
The annual population in Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest states, was expected to grow by 3.8 percent next year from 3.5 percent in 1995. It currently stands at around 16 million.
Asked to comment on child labour in Yemen, Tinstman said:
"Certainly there is a percentage of children who have been exploited in economic activities (here) like in any other country in the world."
But he declined further comment saying UNICEF was working with the government and other public and non-governmental organisations to define the size of child labour in Yemen.
Hundreds of Yemeni children are street vendors while teenagers in rural areas are often forced to skip school because they have to work to help their poor families.

UNICEF's global report on child labour around the world, released in New York on Wednesday, contended that more than 250 million children between 5-14 years were working in conditions detrimental to their health.
